title: No write serialization: concurrent mutations silently lose index entries
description:
Every mutation rewrites the whole .pebbles/index.json with a read-modify-write and a non-atomic std::fs::write (src/storage.rs), with no flock, temp+rename, or transaction. Two overlapping processes therefore produce last-writer-wins on the index while all issue files stay on disk.

Measured on pebbles 1.0.0 (independent runs, throwaway repos in /tmp):
- 10 parallel `pebbles new` with .no_jj: 10 issue files, 9 index entries, 1 permanently invisible orphan, exit 0 for all.
- 6 parallel `pebbles new` in a colocated jj repo: all exit 0 with empty stderr, but jj produced divergent change ids (zvuutynl/0..3, pomyvppy/0..1) plus 4 undescribed working-copy changes; 6 files, 5 index entries, 1 issue not listed.
- Store present but no jj repo: `pebbles new` exits 1 with 'Failed to commit changes: There is no jj repo', yet the issue is written and listed. Exit codes do not describe the store state in either direction.
- A conflicted or otherwise unparseable index.json makes every command fail, including `new`, with 'Failed to parse index file'. No repair command exists (see 0f6f1445 doctor).

ARCHITECTURE.md 'Concurrent Access' (line 416-419) states 'Current design assumes single-user operation. For concurrent use: Jujutsu handles file conflicts automatically'. The measurements above show jj does not handle it usefully: it creates divergent changes and pebbles keeps reporting success.

Ask: serialize mutations per project (advisory lock over index.json taken for the whole read-modify-write plus jj commit), write the index via temp file + rename, detect 'file exists but not in index' and refuse to overwrite silently, and correct the concurrency section of ARCHITECTURE.md to state the real constraint. Related but not covered: epic 0ac66588 (repository graph integrity layer) and its child 0f6f1445 (doctor) cover detection after the fact, not prevention. This matters more now that issue trackers are driven by several concurrent agent sessions per repo.

Decision (owner, 2026-09-22): Option A + write-time stale-index detection. Index writes become atomic temp-file + rename (never torn). At mutation write time, scan .pebbles/issues/ for files newer than the index version READ (baseline = the read index's mtime, not the clock), excluding the current operation's own files; if any are newer, print a warning that the index is stale and should be regenerated (`pebbles reindex`) and continue writing (no refusal). Keep the load-time divergence detection as the backstop. Include exit-code honesty for the store-without-jj-repo case (exit code must match the resulting store state). No lock, no serialization machinery; silent loss becomes a loud, named, repairable condition.
